questions.q: What is a thermodynamic system?
questions.a: A specified quantity of matter or a region in space selected for study.

questions.q: What are surroundings in thermodynamics?
questions.a: Everything outside the system boundary.

questions.q: What separates a system from its surroundings?
questions.a: The system boundary.

questions.q: What is a closed system?
questions.a: A system across whose boundary mass does not cross, although energy may cross.

questions.q: What is an open system?
questions.a: A system across whose boundary both mass and energy can cross.

questions.q: What is an isolated system?
questions.a: An ideal system across whose boundary neither mass nor energy crosses.

questions.q: Name the three basic modes of heat transfer.
questions.a: Conduction, convection and radiation.

questions.q: What is heat transfer?
questions.a: Transfer of thermal energy caused by a temperature difference.

questions.q: Does conduction require a material medium?
questions.a: Yes.

questions.q: What is conduction?
questions.a: Heat transfer through matter by microscopic interactions without bulk motion of the material.

questions.q: State the one-dimensional Fourier conduction relation.
questions.a: Q̇ = −kA(dT/dx).

questions.q: What does k represent in Fourier's law?
questions.a: Thermal conductivity.

questions.q: What does the negative sign in Fourier's law indicate?
questions.a: Heat flows in the direction of decreasing temperature.

questions.q: What is convection?
questions.a: Heat transfer between a surface and a moving fluid.

questions.q: State Newton's law of cooling in the introductory form.
questions.a: Q̇ = hA(Ts − T∞).

questions.q: What does h represent in Newton's law of cooling?
questions.a: The convection heat-transfer coefficient.

questions.q: What is natural or free convection?
questions.a: Convection in which fluid motion is produced by buoyancy effects.

questions.q: What is forced convection?
questions.a: Convection in which fluid motion is driven by a fan, pump or another external device.

questions.q: Can thermal radiation occur through a vacuum?
questions.a: Yes.

questions.q: What is thermal radiation?
questions.a: Energy emitted by matter because of its temperature.

questions.q: State the ideal blackbody emission relation.
questions.a: Eb = σT⁴.

questions.q: On what temperature scale is T used in the blackbody T⁴ relation?
questions.a: Absolute temperature scale (kelvin).

questions.q: What is emissivity?
questions.a: A measure of a real surface's radiative emission relative to an ideal blackbody under the stated conditions.

questions.q: Which heat-transfer mode does not require a material medium?
questions.a: Radiation.

questions.q: What is a heat engine?
questions.a: A cyclic device that converts part of supplied heat into useful work while rejecting remaining heat to a lower-temperature sink.

questions.q: Write the heat-engine net-work relation.
questions.a: Wnet = QH − QL.

questions.q: Write the thermal efficiency of a heat engine.
questions.a: η = Wnet/QH = 1 − QL/QH.

questions.q: What is the high-temperature heat source of a heat engine commonly called?
questions.a: The source or high-temperature reservoir.

questions.q: What is the function of the low-temperature sink in a heat engine?
questions.a: It receives the heat rejected by the engine.

questions.q: What is a refrigerator?
questions.a: A device that uses work input to transfer heat from a low-temperature region to a higher-temperature surrounding.

questions.q: Why does a refrigerator require work input?
questions.a: Because it transfers heat from a lower temperature to a higher temperature, opposite to the natural heat-flow direction.

questions.q: Write the coefficient of performance of a refrigerator.
questions.a: COPR = QL/Wnet.

questions.q: What does a higher refrigerator COP indicate?
questions.a: More cooling effect is obtained per unit of work input under the stated conditions.

questions.q: What is a heat pump?
questions.a: A device using the refrigeration-cycle principle in which the useful effect is heat delivered to the high-temperature space.

questions.q: Write the COP of a heat pump.
questions.a: COPHP = QH/Wnet.

questions.q: State the relation between COP of a heat pump and refrigerator for the same cycle.
questions.a: COPHP = COPR + 1.

questions.q: Name the four main components of a vapour-compression refrigeration system.
questions.a: Compressor, condenser, expansion device and evaporator.

questions.q: What is the function of the compressor in a vapour-compression refrigerator?
questions.a: It raises the pressure of the refrigerant vapour and requires work input.

questions.q: What is the function of the condenser?
questions.a: It rejects heat to the surroundings and moves the high-pressure refrigerant toward the liquid state.

questions.q: What is the function of the expansion device?
questions.a: It reduces the refrigerant pressure.

questions.q: What is the function of the evaporator?
questions.a: It absorbs heat from the refrigerated space.

questions.q: What does HVAC stand for?
questions.a: Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning.

questions.q: Name two major functions of an HVAC system.
questions.a: Temperature control and ventilation; humidity control, filtration and air distribution are also common functions.

questions.q: Why is ventilation important in HVAC systems?
questions.a: It supplies fresh air and helps maintain indoor air quality.

questions.q: What factors besides temperature can affect indoor thermal comfort?
questions.a: Humidity, air movement, air quality, and occupant activity/clothing.

questions.q: Give one engineering application of conduction heat transfer.
questions.a: Heat flow through a metal rod, wall or machine component.

questions.q: Give one engineering application of refrigeration.
questions.a: Domestic refrigeration or cold storage.

questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between heat and work as energy interactions?
questions.a: Heat transfer is caused by a temperature difference, while work is energy transfer associated with a generalised force/displacement interaction other than heat.
